item.title: Resolved gravity wave momentum flux dataset based on the ERA5 reanalysis
item.description:
Resolved gravity wave momentum flux dataset based on the ERA5 reanalysis
Zuzana Procházková and Petr Šácha
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-782,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Energy and momentum are redistributed in the atmosphere by gravity waves. Here, we present a dataset of zonal-mean gravity wave momentum fluxes, a quantity that describes momentum transport. Derived from a reanalysis, the dataset provides information on these waves for 44 years period, with unusually high temporal, vertical and meridional resolution. The data are compared with satellite observation and we illustrate potential use in studying climate effects of gravity waves in the atmosphere.

item.title: A small ensemble of bias-adjusted CMIP6 climate simulations over North America extending to 2300
item.description:
A small ensemble of bias-adjusted CMIP6 climate simulations over North America extending to 2300
Émilie Bresson, Juliette Lavoie, Asli Bese, Anne-Sophie Fortin, David Huard, Travis Logan, and Marco Braun
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-793,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
Even if many sectors would benefit from scientific evidence on the long-term consequences of current policy choices, most climate projections end in 2100. This paper describes a collection of bias-adjusted climate simulations extending to 2300. It includes few Earth System Models, most of them driven by scenarios at the very low or very high end of the range of plausible futures. The composition of the ensemble makes it difficult to deliver climate services supporting climate risk assessments.
